parts.text:
Now use all the given information:
1. model.json file
2. operation.json file
3. Multiview images

Decide which sections of the original model should be modified, removed, interacted with or if new sections should be created. Use as much information from the Multiview images, model.json files and operation.json as possible.

Make this decision from several perspectives. If target clearly identify geometry, locate the corresponding section(s) and face(s) in model.json. If there is no clear geometry identified, use the referenced features and relational_constraint to identify potential sections and features. Additionally, consider the intention of the edit. Based on the function and behavior associated with each section and features, decide which section require the action the most. Then, find the corresponding section and face code from model.json.

Plan out the modeling procedure needed to perform each action. Describe them in professional CAD modelling languages from choosing the plane, draw sketches to extrusion, add chamfers. Be thorough and detailed.

face_code values in model.json are visual labels from shaded renders. Brep_id is the CadQuery Faces() index from the STEP analysis report (for example FACE 0).

Edit operation.json accordingly. Keep the previous request_wording and actions, and add localization plus steps.

OUTPUT FORMAT (JSON, operation.json, no markdown fences, use this schema):
{
  "request": "",
  "request_wording": {
    "action_words": ["..."],
    "referenced_feature_words": ["..."],
    "intention_words": ["..."],
    "grammatical_words": ["..."]
  },
  "actions": [
    {
      "operation": "...",
      "parameters": {
        "parameter_name": "..."
      },
      "target": "...",
      "relational_constraint": "...",
      "unresolved_reference": "...",
      "target section code": ["..."],
      "target face code": ["..."],
      "steps": [
        "...",
        "..."
      ]
    }
  ],
  "intention": ["..."]
}

The model.json, operation.json, and labeled multi-view images follow.

{
  "request": "Mirror the part according to the plane lying on the not rounded end of the part. Merge the mirrored part together with the existing one so they create one body.",
  "request_wording": {
    "action_words": [
      "Mirror",
      "Merge",
      "mirrored"
    ],
    "referenced_feature_words": [
      "part",
      "plane",
      "end",
      "not",
      "rounded",
      "part",
      "part",
      "existing",
      "one",
      "body"
    ],
    "intention_words": [
      "create",
      "one",
      "body"
    ],
    "grammatical_words": [
      "the",
      "according",
      "to",
      "the",
      "lying",
      "on",
      "the",
      "of",
      "the",
      "the",
      "together",
      "with",
      "the",
      "so",
      "they"
    ]
  },
  "actions": [
    {
      "operation": "Mirror (create mirrored copy of the part/body)",
      "parameters": {},
      "target": "the part (current solid body)",
      "relational_constraint": "Mirror according to the plane lying on the not rounded end of the part (mirror plane coincident with that end plane/face)",
      "unresolved_reference": "Identify the plane/planar face located on the not-rounded end of the part to use as the mirror plane (which specific end face/plane is meant)."
    },
    {
      "operation": "Merge/Boolean union (combine bodies into one)",
      "parameters": {},
      "target": "mirrored part + existing part",
      "relational_constraint": "Merge together with the existing one so they create one body (result must be a single solid body)",
      "unresolved_reference": "Confirm the merge scope includes exactly the original body and the newly mirrored body; ensure join/union is intended even if contact is only along the mirror plane."
    }
  ],
  "intention": [
    "Create a symmetric version of the part about the end plane and ensure the result is a single unified solid body."
  ]
}
